citation.title: New trends in microwave imaging diagnostics and application to burning plasma
citation.authors: Y. Zhu, J.-H. Yu, M. Chen, B. Tobias, N.C. Luhmann Jr.
citation.pages: 2110-2130 (from supplied citation hint; not visible in extracted text)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1109/TPS.2019.2911476 (identifier hint; not printed in the extracted text, unverified)

topic: Tutorial review of microwave diagnostics: ECE, ECEI, MIR, synthetic diagnostics, SoC receivers, wide-bandgap electronics, and imaging optics.
own_question: How microwave imaging diagnostics work, and which hardware and modelling advances extend them toward burning plasmas.
actual_method_and_evidence: Narrative tutorial. It reviews cold-plasma dispersion, ECE optical depth, and reflectometry phase relations, then summarizes published ECEI and MIR observations from several devices, including KSTAR MIR hardware. It also describes synthetic-diagnostic forward modelling and an LCP ECEI module cross-calibrated against Thomson scattering on DIII-D. It contains no CES or ion-temperature content and no nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: ECEI passively measures 2D electron-temperature fluctuations, and relative fluctuation analysis does not require absolute calibration. This is electron information, not impurity-ion temperature.
claim_checks.qualification: Relies on the optically thick assumption. Our inputs are uncalibrated ECEI voltage snapshots.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. No CES, no report timing, no 10 ms grid.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable. The cited synthetic-diagnostic correlation threshold of 0.6 belongs to MIR design, not to our validation designs.
forbidden_inferences: ECEI measures ion or carbon-impurity temperature
This source shows that ECEI predicts CES temperature
The described KSTAR hardware matches the KSTAR2022 configuration
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional background citation only, for the nature of ECEI electron-temperature signals. It is not evidence for ion-temperature nowcasting, and a dedicated ECEI or BES reference would serve better.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
